introduction: These hundred readings speak of love as a fire: one that burns away veils, warms the cold, gives light as a lamp does, and consumes everything in the lover but the Beloved. Beside them stand passages from other scriptures and from poets and philosophers who used the same picture, among them the burning bush, the coal on Isaiah's lips, the tongues of fire at Pentecost, Sa‘di's moth and Rumi's reed, together with voices that distrust fire: the Buddha, for whom the world is aflame and freedom is the flame going out, Friar Laurence, the Stoics, and Elijah's still small voice. They are set there to ask what kind of fire this is, what it burns, and how it is kept.
questions: The readings speak of a fire that burns away veils. What, in your experience, stands between a person and what they love most?
The Buddha and the Dhammapada treat fire as the passions that must be put out. How does the fire of love in these readings differ from the fire they mean?
Several passages warn of zeal without knowledge and of a tongue that sets things ablaze. How can ardour be kept from harming others?
The readings on separation speak of a burning that does not end. What makes longing bearable, and what does it produce in a person?
Leviticus asks that the fire on the altar never go out, and Jesus foresees love growing cold. What practices keep a person's love alive over many years?
Where have you seen one person's warmth kindle another's?

outside.why: The Letter to the Hebrews tells its readers to serve with reverence, for our God is a consuming fire.

In the Fire Sermon the Buddha tells his monks that the eye, the mind and all they touch are aflame, and that freedom lies in the fire going out. Which fires in a person should be fed, and which put out?
The two disciples at Emmaus said afterwards: did not our heart burn within us while he talked with us by the way?
At Sinai Moses saw a bush that burned with fire and was not consumed.
John the Baptist said that the one coming after him would baptize with the Holy Ghost and with fire.
The Qur’an tells how Moses saw a fire from afar and said to his family: wait, I see a fire.
Proverbs asks whether a man can take fire in his bosom and his clothes not be burned. What does it take to carry a consuming flame with patience and composure?
Malachi says that the messenger of the covenant is like a refiner's fire, who shall purify as gold and silver are purified.
The Light Verse of the Qur’an speaks of an oil that would almost glow though no fire touched it.
At Pentecost tongues like as of fire sat upon each of the disciples, and they began to speak.
John Wesley wrote that at a quarter before nine one evening he felt his heart strangely warmed.
The Song of Songs says that love is strong as death, and its coals are coals of fire.
The Dhammapada says that there is no fire like passion, and no happiness higher than rest. Is the fire of love another passion to be quieted, or what burns the passions away?
A seraph touched Isaiah's lips with a live coal from the altar, and his iniquity was taken away.
Plato's Socrates argues that the madness of love is the greatest of heaven's blessings.
Paul says that love bears all things and endures all things, and never fails.
Spinoza describes an intellectual love of God that is calm and without passion. Must love be fire to be love?
Dante ends his poem with the love which moves the sun and the other stars.
Thomas à Kempis says that love makes every heavy thing light and bears evenly every uneven thing.
The Dhammapada says that the scent of good people travels even against the wind.
Jesus said that a city set on a hill cannot be hid.
Proverbs has another picture from the forge: iron sharpeneth iron, and so one person another.
The psalmist says: my heart was hot within me; while I was musing the fire burned.
Lamentations says that the Lord's compassions fail not; they are new every morning.
Paul writes that he was taken from his friends in presence, not in heart.
Friar Laurence warns two lovers that violent delights have violent ends, like fire and powder, which as they kiss consume. How is an intense longing kept from burning itself out?
The psalm asks to be taught to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
Jeremiah tried to keep silent, and the word was in his heart as a burning fire shut up in his bones.
Paul said of some that they had a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge. What must a teacher's fire be joined with?
Jesus told Nicodemus that one must be born of water and of the Spirit.
Leviticus commands that the fire on the altar shall ever be burning; it shall never go out.
Sa‘di tells the nightingale to learn love from the moth, which burned, lost its life, and found no voice.
Paul asks the Romans to be fervent in spirit, serving the Lord.
Jeremiah hears: is not my word like as a fire, and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?
James warns that the tongue is a fire, and that a little fire kindles a great matter. What distinguishes speech that melts hearts from speech that sets them against each other?
Paul reminds Timothy to stir up the gift that is in him.
Elijah found that the Lord was not in the wind, the earthquake or the fire, but in a still small voice. When does a quiet word do what fire cannot?
Paul says it in three words to the church at Thessalonica: quench not the Spirit.
Proverbs says that the path of the just shines more and more unto the perfect day.
Israel was led through the wilderness by a pillar of fire that gave them light by night.
Paul hopes that his friends will shine as lights in the world.
The psalmist says: the zeal of Thine house hath eaten me up.
On Carmel the fire of the Lord fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the water in the trench.
Isaiah hears the promise: when thou passest through the waters I will be with thee, and through the fire thou shalt not be burned.
Paul says that every man's work shall be revealed by fire, which shall try it.
The Song of Songs opens with the words of the beloved: thy love is better than wine.
Plato describes the lover who climbs from one beautiful thing to another and suddenly perceives a nature of wondrous beauty.
Julian of Norwich was told that love was her Lord's meaning in everything he showed her.
Donne asks God to break, blow and burn him, and make him new.
Francis Thompson fled a pursuing love down the nights and down the days.
Locke insisted that reason must be our last judge and guide in everything. What becomes of judgment in a valley where reason is said to have no place?
Pascal wrote that the heart has its reasons, which reason does not know.
Hume held that reason is the slave of the passions and can only serve them. Is the lover who burns the harvest of reason giving up reason, or putting it to its proper use?
Donne told the one he was leaving that their two souls endure not a breach but an expansion, like gold beaten thin.
The lover in the Song of Songs rises at night and goes about the streets seeking the one her soul loves.
The crowd at Pentecost said of the disciples: these men are full of new wine.
Marcus Aurelius wished to be like a headland on which the waves break while it stands unmoved. Which is the better picture of a good life: the unmoved rock or the one who is possessed?
Jesus said that whoever loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him.
Ignatius of Antioch, going to his death, called himself God's wheat, to be ground into pure bread.
The church at Laodicea is told: I would thou wert cold or hot.
Rumi asks when he was ever made less by dying: as mineral he died and became a plant, as animal he died and was a man.
Proverbs says that good news from a far country is as cold waters to a thirsty soul.
The first letter of Peter tells its readers not to think the fiery trial strange.
On the mountain the face of Jesus shone as the sun before three of his disciples.
The Qur’an says that when Abraham was cast into the fire, God said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham.
The psalmist says that his soul thirsts and his flesh longs in a dry and thirsty land.
Augustine says to God: too late did I love Thee, O Beauty so ancient and so new.
Paul says: I live, yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.
Jesus foresaw a time when the love of many would wax cold. What cools a fire once lit, and how is it tended?
The elder writes that he has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth.
The church at Ephesus is praised for its labour and told: thou hast left thy first love. How does a person known for ardour keep it from becoming a reputation?
The psalmist's soul pants after God as the hart after the water brooks.
The psalmist asks that his tears be put into God's bottle, and written in His book.
Rumi's reed-flute has lamented ever since it was cut from the reed-bed, and its music is the fire of that longing.
By the rivers of Babylon the exiles sat down and wept when they remembered Zion.
The Dhammapada concludes from the pain of loss that one should love nothing, since those who love nothing have no fetters. Is the fire of separation a reason to love less?
The Song of Songs says: my beloved is mine, and I am his.
Tennyson held it true, whatever befell, that it is better to have loved and lost than never to have loved at all.
Epictetus taught: never say of anything, I have lost it, but, I have returned it. Does that calm honour the one who is gone, or deny what was felt?
The psalmist asks his own soul why it is cast down, and tells it to hope in God.
The darkest of the psalms ends: lover and friend hast Thou put far from me.
Jesus said: I am come to send fire on the earth, and what will I, if it be already kindled?
The Song of Songs says that many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.
The Qur’an says that they would put out the light of God with their mouths, but God will perfect His light.
Augustine says that our hearts are restless until they rest in God.
Tertullian told the persecutors of his day that the blood of Christians is seed.
Nietzsche replied to all such claims that blood is the very worst witness to truth. What does the willingness to die for love show, and what does it not?
Polycarp, threatened with the fire, answered that he had served his King eighty-six years and would not deny Him.
Paul says that though he give his body to be burned and have not love, it profits nothing. What in a martyr's fire is the love, and what only the burning?
In the Book of Daniel three men walk unharmed in the furnace, and a fourth with them.
Isaiah calls to a people in darkness: arise, shine, for thy light is come.
Ezekiel hears the promise of a new heart: the stony heart taken away and a heart of flesh given.
James asks believers to pray for one another, and says such prayer avails much.
Rabi‘a prayed: if I worship Thee for fear of hell, burn me in hell, and if in hope of paradise, shut me out of it. What is the fire of love asked for, if not for reward?
The psalmist prays: create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit.
Simeon said of the child that he was set for the fall and rising again of many.
Hopkins wrote that the grandeur of God will flame out, like shining from shook foil.
Israel said at Sinai: we have heard His voice out of the midst of the fire.
The Qur’an says that in the remembrance of God hearts find rest.
Tagore tells the worshipper to leave his chanting and telling of beads, for God is with the tiller and the path-maker. Is the warmth of remembrance found in devotion, or in work beside others?

isaiah-live-coal.text: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged

psalm-while-i-was-musing.text: My heart was hot within me, while I was musing the fire burned: then spake I with my tongue

hebrews-consuming-fire.text: Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear: For our God is a consuming fire

leviticus-fire-ever-burning.text: The fire shall ever be burning upon the altar; it shall never go out

kings-fire-of-the-lord-fell.text: Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he is the God

timothy-stir-up-the-gift.text: Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands. For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind

proverbs-fire-in-his-bosom.text: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned

matthew-love-of-many-shall-wax-cold.text: And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold

romans-fervent-in-spirit.text: Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord

song-many-waters-cannot-quench.text: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned

psalm-zeal-of-thine-house.text: For the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up; and the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me

acts-cloven-tongues-of-fire.text: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance

quran-i-perceive-a-fire.text: When he saw a fire and said unto his folk: Lo! Wait! I see a fire afar off. Peradventure I may bring you a brand therefrom or may find guidance at the fire.

shakespeare-violent-delights.text: These violent delights have violent ends / And in their triumph die, like fire and powder, / Which as they kiss consume
shakespeare-violent-delights.author: William Shakespeare

source.label: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (MIT)

buddha-all-is-aflame.text: Monks, the All is aflame. What All is aflame? The eye is aflame. Forms are aflame. Consciousness at the eye is aflame. Contact at the eye is aflame
buddha-all-is-aflame.work: Adittapariyaya Sutta (Samyutta Nikaya 35.28), the Fire Sermon

rights.note: Modern translation, offered for free distribution; a brief extract.

dhammapada-no-fire-like-passion.text: There is no fire like passion; there is no losing throw like hatred; there is no pain like this body; there is no happiness higher than rest

plato-madness-of-love.text: the madness of love is the greatest of heaven's blessings
plato-madness-of-love.author: Plato

saadi-learn-love-from-the-moth.text: O bird of the morning, learn love from the moth Because it burnt, lost its life, and found no voice. These pretenders are ignorantly in search of Him, Because he who obtained knowledge has not returned
saadi-learn-love-from-the-moth.author: Saʿdī

gita-flame-of-knowledge.text: As the kindled flame Feeds on the fuel till it sinks to ash
